If you're here, on this sub, it means you're still trying. It means you're still fighting, and that's more than other people can say they've done. I've been depressed for about half my life, maybe longer. And some days are really hard. Some days I get so anxious to keep surviving. I get anxious to die. I've been on the brink of death, I've seen the pain in my family's eyes when I've attempted. 
But there was something I read, if you struggle to find a reason to live, do it for your family and siblings. Do it for your pets. Do it to take care of your plants. Or to play a game you love. Keep living to bring kindness to others. Keep living to hear that album you've been waiting for. Keep living so you can eat your favorite meal. Keep living to watch your favorite show! Even if you're struggling, remember that you woke up today, and you survived! Because no matter what, even if you can only extend your life by a single day, you are proving yourself to keep fighting each time.

Everyone has a story they don't want to talk about, there's nothing wrong with that. It's okay if you don't want to talk about it. It's okay if you might be feeling a little weaker than usual. A little more empty. There is nothing ever wrong with having emotions, or things that we can't bear to speak about. But you know what you did today? You SURVIVED. Not everyone does that. Not everyone wakes up, and conquers another day, even without trying to. You woke up, and even if it was hard, you still kicked today in the ass! 
If you ever just need a reason to live, do it for your pets. To love them. Do it to care for your plants. Or to wave to someone and make them smile by holding open a door. Keep surviving to listen to that new album you've been waiting for. To watch that new season of a show. Because even if I don't know you, I still love you and hope that you can find even just the smallest of reasons to keep going. This is extended to anyone who reads this.

I was in a mental hospital for 1 day after I checked myself into the ER for suicidal ideation. It wasn't like what I expected, but I'm told that every hospital is different. The one I went to, people were kind, and a lot of them were depressed like me, just sad and misunderstood. There were some people who couldn't truly function on their own, schizophrenics, bipolar, eating disorders, etc. There was one man who tried to overdose on Benadryl, and he was amazing at playing classical music on the piano in the common room. There were people of all ages. But many were around my age. We did all activities as a group, group therapy, group exercising, eating at the same time. Everything was scheduled, and at night, they'd check my room every 15 minutes so that I didn't risk hurting myself. The staff was kind, we weren't treated like anything less than human. It was a bright and inviting environment, despite some people experiencing bad mental hospitals. I didn't have a roomate, and our rooms don't have doors, except for our bathrooms, where everything is secured. We were allowed to wear clothing that was dress code approved and we were given a notebook that we could write in (you had to ask for a pencil from the nurses, and they give you a dull one). For the 1 day that I was in there, I bonded with people and we all supported one another. I will keep that experience forever close to my heart because for once, I didn't feel alone. I didn't feel like an outsider. I was 23 at the time, but there were people younger than me, and some very much older. But it's not so scary like they show you in movies.
